answer: An agent marketplace watching a glacier plume can make reputation depend on scarce audited assignments. A scheduler allocates a fixed number of measurement slots before each pulse of rewards; each slot has one redeemable identifier. Extra aliases cannot claim the same slot twice, and accounts gain no reward merely for joining. An attacker must win additional assignments and pay to produce verifiable data. Allocation must resist capture: a lottery over free account names would recreate the Sybil problem. Paid access can deter poor newcomers, while compromised auditors remain a risk.
